1364.10: The saloks of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O Kabir, my rosary is (my) tongue, on which is (the Name of) Ram. From the beginning, from the start of the ages, he has been the peace and resting place of all the devotees. ॥1॥
1364.11: O Kabir, everyone laughs at my caste; (but) I am a sacrifice to this caste, in which (born, I) have repeated the Name of the Creator. ॥2॥
1364.12: O Kabir, why do you waver? Why do you let your soul be shaken? Drink the sweet essence of the Name of Ram, the master of all comforts. ॥3॥
1364.13: O Kabir, (if) earrings are made of gold, with rubies set in them, (still, on) those in whose mind the Name is not, (the earrings) look like burnt reeds. ॥4॥
1364.14: O Kabir, rare is such a one, hardly one or two, who is dead while yet alive, and, become fearless, sings the praises (of God); wherever I look, there he is. ॥5॥
1364.15: O Kabir, the day I died (to self), after that came bliss; I met my God, and (now my) companions (too) worship Gobind. ॥6॥
1364.16: O Kabir, I am the worst of all; everyone but me is good. Whoever has come to understand (himself) so is my friend. ॥7॥
1364.17: O Kabir, (Maya, the world's illusion and lure,) came to me in many guises; (but) my Guru saved me, and she bowed (to me). ॥8॥
1364.18: O Kabir, let us kill only that (Haumai, ego) whose death brings peace; everyone calls (its killing) good, good; no one takes (it) as bad. ॥9॥
1364.19: O Kabir, the nights are dark, and the black-(hearted) creatures rise up; taking nooses, they rise and run out; know that they are struck down by God. ॥10॥
1365.1: O Kabir, (even) a small sandalwood plant is good, (though) it is hemmed in by dhaak and palaas trees; they too, who dwell near the sandalwood, become sandalwood. ॥11॥
1365.2: O Kabir, the bamboo is drowned in (the pride of) its greatness; let no one drown like this. The bamboo dwells near the sandalwood, (yet) it does not become fragrant. ॥12॥
1365.3: O Kabir, (man) lost his deen (the way of God) for the sake of the world, (but) the world did not go with (him). The heedless one struck his own foot with an axe, by his own hand. ॥13॥
1365.4: O Kabir, wherever I have wandered, (I saw) spectacles in place after place; (but) without one who loves Ram, (it is all) a wilderness in my eyes. ॥14॥
1365.5: O Kabir, the hut of the Sants is good; the village of the false is a furnace. Let fire take that mansion in which there is not the Name of the Lord. ॥15॥
1365.6: O Kabir, why weep when a Sant dies? He goes to his own home. Weep for the wretched Saakat (one who has turned from God), who is sold from shop to shop. ॥16॥
1365.7: O Kabir, the Saakat is like a store of garlic; eat it sitting in a corner, (yet) in the end it becomes known. ॥17॥
1365.8: O Kabir, Maya is the churning pot, and the breath is the churner; the Sants have eaten the butter, (while) the world drinks the buttermilk. ॥18॥
1365.9: O Kabir, Maya is the churning pot, and the breath flows like a cool stream; the one who churned has eaten (the butter); the others are (only) churning. ॥19॥
1365.10: O Kabir, Maya is a thief, who robs and robs (people) and stocks (her) shop; Kabir alone is not robbed (by her), for he has cut her into twelve pieces. ॥20॥
1365.11: O Kabir, in this world there is no peace (for those) who make many friends; those who keep their mind on the One find peace always. ॥21॥
1365.12: O Kabir, the death the world fears (brings) joy to my mind; only by dying is the perfect, supreme Bliss (God) found. ॥22॥
1365.13: Having found the treasure of Ram, O Kabir, do not untie its bundle; (for it) there is no market, no assayer, no buyer, no price. ॥23॥
1365.14: O Kabir, love the one whose Master is Ram; pandits, kings and lords of the land, of what use are they? ॥24॥
1365.15: O Kabir, by loving the One, every other duality goes; whether you grow your hair long, or shave (your head) bare. ॥25॥
1365.16: O Kabir, the world is a chamber of soot; the blind have fallen into it. I am a sacrifice to those who, having entered, come out (again). ॥26॥
1365.17: O Kabir, this body will go; if you can, turn it back. Those who had hundreds of thousands and tens of millions departed barefoot. ॥27॥
1365.18: O Kabir, this body will go; set it on some (good) path: either keep the company of the Saadh (the holy one), or sing the praises of the Lord. ॥28॥
1365.19: O Kabir, dying and dying, the whole world has died, yet no one has known even how to die. One who dies such a death will not die again. ॥29॥
1366.1: O Kabir, human birth is hard to obtain; it does not come again and again; as the fruits of the forest, once ripe, fall to the ground and are not joined to the branch again. ॥30॥
1366.2: O Kabir, (say, O Lord,) you alone are Kabir (the Great); your Name is Kabir. The jewel of Ram is found only when (you) first give up (attachment to) the body. ॥31॥
Kabir is an Arabic word meaning great; al-Kabir (the Great) is a name of God.
1366.3: O Kabir, let us not fret and complain; nothing comes of what you say. The favours that Kareem (the Gracious Lord) bestows, no one can erase. ॥32॥
1366.4: O Kabir, (on) the touchstone of Ram no false one can stand. The touchstone of Ram is borne only by one who has died and come alive. ॥33॥
1366.5: O Kabir, (people) wear white clothes and chew betel and areca nut; (but) without the Name of the one Lord, they go bound to the city of Jam (the messenger of Death). ॥34॥
1366.6: O Kabir, the boat is rotten, with thousands of holes burst open; the light ones have floated across; those with loads on their heads have drowned. ॥35॥
1366.7: O Kabir, the bones burn as wood does, and the hair as grass; seeing this world burning, Kabir has grown detached. ॥36॥
1366.8: O Kabir, one should not be proud: (the body is but) bones wrapped in skin. Those (who rode) on fine horses, under royal canopies, were at last buried in the earth too. ॥37॥
1366.9: O Kabir, one should not be proud, seeing one's lofty house; today or tomorrow (you) will lie on the ground, and grass will grow over (you). ॥38॥
1366.10: O Kabir, one should not be proud, nor laugh at anyone poor; (your) boat is still out at sea: what do I know of what may happen? ॥39॥
1366.11: O Kabir, one should not be proud, seeing one's fair body; today or tomorrow (you) will leave it behind, as a snake its slough. ॥40॥
1366.12: O Kabir, if you would plunder, plunder now: the Name of Ram is there to be plundered; or else you will repent later, (when) the breath of life slips away. ॥41॥
1366.13: O Kabir, no one has been born such as would set fire to his own house, and, burning the five sons, remain lovingly attuned to Ram. ॥42॥
The five sons are the five passions: lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride.
1366.14: Is there anyone who would sell (his) son, and sell (his) daughter, go into partnership with Kabir, and trade with the Lord? ॥43॥
1366.15: O Kabir, (I give you) this warning, lest any doubt remain (in your mind): for the pleasures (you) have enjoyed till now, take (a little) molasses in exchange and eat it. ॥44॥
1366.16: O Kabir, I had thought that reading was good; (but) better than reading is union (with God); I will not give up devotion to Ram, even if people slander (me). ॥45॥
1366.17: O Kabir, why should the poor people slander, who have no wisdom in their mind? Kabir is absorbed in Ram, and has given up all other work. ॥46॥
1366.18: O Kabir, on all four sides fire has caught the robe of the stranger (soul); the patched coat (of the body) has burnt to charcoal, but the thread (of the soul) was not touched by the flame. ॥47॥
The khintha is the patched coat that yogis wear.
1366.19: O Kabir, the patched coat has burnt to charcoal, and the begging bowl is smashed to pieces; the wretched yogi's play is over; only ashes are left on his seat. ॥48॥
The khapar is the yogi's begging bowl, and the bibhut the ash he smears on his body.
1367.1: O Kabir, the fish is in shallow water, and the fisherman has cast his net; (O fish,) in this little pool you will not escape; turn back and make for the ocean. ॥49॥
1367.2: O Kabir, one should not forsake the ocean, even if its water is very salty; no one will call good one who searches from pond to pond. ॥50॥
1367.3: O Kabir, those without a master (without a Guru) are swept away; there is no one to hold them. (Those who) have made meekness and humility their own (accept that) what comes from the Creator comes. ॥51॥
1367.4: O Kabir, the dog of a Vaishnav (the true devotee) is good, the mother of a Saakat is bad; the one hears the praise of the Lord's Name every day, (while) the other goes out to buy sin. ॥52॥
1367.5: O Kabir, the deer is weak, and this pool is lush and green; the hunters are a hundred thousand, the life one: how long can I escape death? ॥53॥
1367.6: O Kabir, (those) who make their home on the bank of the Ganga, and drink its pure water, without devotion to the Lord (even they) are not liberated; so saying, Kabir dwells on Ram. ॥54॥
1367.7: O Kabir, (my) mind has become pure, like the water of the Ganga; (now) the Lord follows behind (me), calling, Kabir, Kabir. ॥55॥
1367.8: O Kabir, turmeric is yellow, and lime is white in hue; the lover of Ram meets (Ram) only when both colours (both castes) are lost. ॥56॥
1367.9: O Kabir, turmeric loses its yellowness, and no trace of the lime's white remains; I am a sacrifice to this love, through which caste, colour and lineage depart. ॥57॥
1367.10: O Kabir, the door of liberation is narrow, a tenth part of a mustard seed; but the mind has become a maddened elephant: how can it pass through? ॥58॥
1367.11: O Kabir, if such a True Guru is met, who, well pleased, shows his grace, then the door of liberation is wide, and I come and go (through it) with ease. ॥59॥
1367.12: O Kabir, I have no thatch and no hut, I have no house and no village; perhaps the Lord will ask who this is; I have neither caste nor name. ॥60॥
1367.13: O Kabir, I long to die; and if I die, (let it be) at the Lord's door; perhaps the Lord will ask who this is, lying at my door. ॥61॥
1367.14: O Kabir, I have not done (anything), nor shall I do, nor can (this) body do (anything); what do I know? Whatever (was done), the Lord did, and Kabir became Kabir. ॥62॥
1367.15: O Kabir, one from whose mouth Ram comes forth, even when babbling in a dream, (let) the shoes on his feet (be made) of the skin of my body. ॥63॥
1367.16: O Kabir, we are puppets of clay, (yet we) have given (ourselves) the name of man; (we are) guests for four days, (yet) we take up great, great places. ॥64॥
1367.17: O Kabir, making myself henna, I toiled, having myself ground and ground (fine); (but) you, O Husband Lord, did not ask after (me), and never put (me) to your feet. ॥65॥
1367.18: O Kabir, the door where no one stops (us), coming or going, how can one leave a door that is such? ॥66॥
1367.19: O Kabir, I was drowning, but was saved, lifted in a flash by a wave of (God's) virtues; when I saw that the boat was rotten, I leapt and got off (it). ॥67॥
1368.1: O Kabir, devotion does not please the sinner, nor does the worship of the Lord appeal to him; the fly forsakes the sandalwood, and goes where there is a stench. ॥68॥
1368.2: O Kabir, the physician has died, the patient has died, the whole world has died; Kabir alone has not died, for whom there is no one to weep. ॥69॥
1368.3: O Kabir, Ram was not meditated on, (and so) a heavy rot has set in; the body is a wooden pot: it cannot be set (on the fire) again. ॥70॥
1368.4: O Kabir, it has come about that (I) have done what my mind loved; why fear death, once (the sati) has taken the vermilion-smeared coconut in her hand? ॥71॥
A woman resolved to become a sati, to burn on her husband's pyre, took a vermilion-smeared coconut (sidhaura) in her hand, the sign that she did not fear death.
1368.5: O Kabir, the cane is sucked for its juice; for virtues one must weep and die. No one will call good a man full of faults. ॥72॥
1368.6: O Kabir, the pitcher is full of water; today or tomorrow (it) will break. Those who do not remember their Guru will be robbed halfway (on the road). ॥73॥
1368.7: O Kabir, I am the dog of Ram; Moti is my name; around my neck is a rope: wherever (he) pulls, there (I) go. ॥74॥
1368.8: O Kabir, why do you show the world your rosary of wood? (If) you do not remember Ram in your heart, what use is this rosary? ॥75॥
1368.9: O Kabir, (in whose) mind the serpent of separation dwells, on (him) no charm works; one parted from Ram does not live; and if he lives, he goes mad. ॥76॥
1368.10: O Kabir, the paaras and the sandalwood have one quality in common: meeting them, even iron and scentless wood become excellent. ॥77॥
1368.11: O Kabir, the club of Jam is terrible: it cannot be endured; (but) I met a Saadh, and he took me to the hem (of his robe). ॥78॥
1368.12: O Kabir, the physician says: I alone am good; the cure is in my hands; (but) this (life) is the property of Gopal (the sustainer of the world): when it pleases (him), (he) takes it back. ॥79॥
1368.13: O Kabir, beat your own drum for ten days; like the meeting (of passengers) in a river boat, (this meeting) will not come again. ॥80॥
1368.14: O Kabir, if I make the seven seas ink, and make all the plants pens, and make the earth paper, (still) the praise of the Lord cannot be written. ॥81॥
1368.15: O Kabir, what (harm) can (my) caste, the weaver's, do, (when) Gopal dwells in (my) heart? O Kabir, meet the all-pervading Lord in his embrace, and all entanglements will end. ॥82॥
1368.16: O Kabir, there is no one such as would burn down (his) house, and, killing the five sons, remain lovingly attuned to Ram. ॥83॥
1368.17: O Kabir, there is no one such as would set fire to (his attachment to) this body; the blind world does not understand, (though) Kabir keeps crying it aloud. ॥84॥
1368.18: O Kabir, the sati, mounted on the pyre, cries out: Listen, O brother cremation ground: all the people have gone away; in the end it is you and I who have business together. ॥85॥
1369.1: O Kabir, the mind has become a bird; it flies and flies off in the ten directions; whatever company one finds, such is the fruit one eats. ॥86॥
1369.2: O Kabir, the place I was searching for, that very place I have found; you have turned and become the very One whom you used to call another. ॥87॥
1369.3: O Kabir, I am dying, struck down by bad company, like a banana plant that stands near a jujube tree; the one (the jujube) sways, and the other (the banana) is torn; do not look toward the company of a Saakat. ॥88॥
1369.4: O Kabir, others' load keeps mounting on (a man's) head, and (still) he wants to walk the road; he does not fear his own load, (though) ahead lies a hard and treacherous pass. ॥89॥
1369.5: O Kabir, the burnt wood of the forest stands and cries out: may I not fall into the blacksmith's hands, (for he) will burn (me) a second time. ॥90॥
1369.6: O Kabir, when one died, two died; when two died, four; when four died, six died: four males and two females. ॥91॥
A riddle: when the one (the mind) dies, the vices that live by it die with it.
1369.7: O Kabir, I searched the world, looking and looking, (but) nowhere found a place (of rest); those who have not remembered the Name of the Lord, why do they stray off elsewhere? ॥92॥
1369.8: O Kabir, let us keep the company of the Saadh, (which) stands by us to the end; one should not keep the company of a Saakat, from which comes ruin. ॥93॥
1369.9: O Kabir, (those who) in this world remembered (God), knowing that he pervades the world, (have made their birth fruitful); those who have not remembered the Name of the Lord were born in vain. ॥94॥
1369.10: O Kabir, let us place our hope in Ram; hope in others (ends) in despair. Those men who turn away from the Name of the Lord fall into hell. ॥95॥
1369.11: O Kabir, (they) made many disciples and followers, (but) did not make Keshav (the Lord) their friend; (they) had set out to meet the Lord, (but their) mind got stuck on the way. ॥96॥
1369.12: O Kabir, what can the poor creature do, if Ram (himself) gives no help? Whatever branch I set my foot on bends and bends (and breaks). ॥97॥
1369.13: O Kabir, those who preach to others, sand falls into (their own) mouths; they guard the wealth of others, (while) the field of their own home has been eaten up. ॥98॥
1369.14: O Kabir, (let me) stay in the company of the Saadh, (even if I) eat barley husks; what is to be will be; (but let me) not go in the company of Saakats. ॥99॥
1369.15: O Kabir, in the company of the Saadh, love doubles day by day; the Saakat is a black blanket, which does not become white though it is washed. ॥100॥
1369.16: O Kabir, you have not shaved your mind; why have you had your hair shaved off? Whatever was done, the mind did; shaving the head is useless. ॥101॥
1369.17: O Kabir, one should not forsake Ram; (if) body and wealth go, let them go; (my) mind is pierced by the lotus feet (of the Lord); (let me) remain merged in the Name of Ram. ॥102॥
1369.18: O Kabir, the instrument I used to play, all its strings have snapped; what can the poor instrument do? The player has departed. ॥103॥
1369.19: O Kabir, I would shave the head of the mother of that guru by whom doubt is not dispelled; (such gurus) are drowned themselves in the four Vedas, and have swept away (their) disciples (too). ॥104॥
To shave someone's mother's head is an old curse of disgrace.
1370.1: O Kabir, whatever sins were committed were kept hidden beneath; (but) in the end they all came to light when Dharam Raj (the judge of souls) asked. ॥105॥
1370.2: O Kabir, giving up the remembrance of the Lord, (man) raised a large family; busy with his affairs, he passed away, and neither brother nor kinsman remained. ॥106॥
1370.3: O Kabir, (the woman) who, giving up the remembrance of the Lord, goes at night to rouse (the spirits of the cremation ground) is born a she-serpent, and eats her own offspring. ॥107॥
1370.4: O Kabir, the woman who, giving up the remembrance of the Lord, keeps the fast of Ahoi (the goddess Sitala) is born a she-donkey, and bears a load of four maunds. ॥108॥
1370.5: O Kabir, the very greatest wisdom is (this): repeat the Name of the Lord within your heart; (but this) is play on top of a stake: if (one) falls, there is no resting place. ॥109॥
1370.6: O Kabir, blessed is that mouth with which Ram is uttered; what to say of the poor body? The whole village will be made pure. ॥110॥
1370.7: O Kabir, good is that family in which (is born) a servant of the Lord; the family in which no servant (of the Lord) is born is (like) the dhaak and palaas trees. ॥111॥
1370.8: O Kabir, (though there be) horses, elephants and carriages in countless throngs, (and) a hundred thousand banners flying, better than this comfort is begging, if (one's) days pass in remembering the Lord. ॥112॥
1370.9: O Kabir, I have wandered the whole world, with a drum slung on my shoulder; no one belongs to anyone: I have seen all, tapping and sounding them out. ॥113॥
1370.10: Pearls lie scattered on the path, and a blind man has come along; without the light of Jagdish (the Lord of the world), the world passes over (them). ॥114॥
1370.11: The line of Kabir is drowned, (now that) the son Kamal is born: giving up the remembrance of the Lord, (he) has brought wealth home. ॥115॥
By tradition, Kamal was Kabir's son.
1370.12: O Kabir, when you go to meet the Saadh, take no one with you; do not set your foot back; whatever comes ahead, let it come. ॥116॥
1370.13: O Kabir, with the rope by which the world is bound, do not be bound, O Kabir; (or) your body, like gold, will be lost, as salt in flour. ॥117॥
1370.14: O Kabir, the swan (the soul) is about to fly, the body about to be buried, (yet the mortal) gives instructions by signs; even now the creature does not give up the greed of its eyes. ॥118॥
1370.15: O Kabir, (say, O Lord,) let me behold you with my eyes, and hear your Name with my ears; let me utter your Name with my tongue, and (keep your) lotus feet in my heart. ॥119॥
1370.16: O Kabir, by the grace of the True Guru, I have been spared both heaven and hell; (now,) from the beginning to the end, I dwell in the joy of the lotus feet (of the Lord). ॥120॥
1370.17: O Kabir, how can the joy of the lotus feet be told or measured? (Its) glory does not lie in the telling; it is believed only when it is seen. ॥121॥
1370.18: O Kabir, having seen (him), to whom shall I tell it? No one believes what is told. The Lord is as he is, he alone; (let me) dwell in joy, singing (his) praises. ॥122॥
1371.1: O Kabir, (the kunj, the demoiselle crane,) pecks her feed and remembers (her young), pecks again, and, pecking and pecking, remembers (them); as the kunj (keeps) her young (in mind), so, O brother, the mind (holds) its attachment to Maya. ॥123॥
1371.2: O Kabir, the sky is overcast with cloud, and its rain has filled the ponds and lakes; (those) who (still) go thirsting like the chatrik (rain-bird), what will be their state? ॥124॥
1371.3: O Kabir, if the chakvi (the ruddy sheldrake) is parted (from her mate) at night, she comes and meets (him) at dawn; (but) those who are parted from Ram meet (him) neither by day nor by night. ॥125॥
1371.4: O Kabir, O conch, parted from Ratnakar (the ocean, the mine of jewels), stay in the ocean; (or else) at every sunrise you will wail in temple after temple. ॥126॥
1371.5: O Kabir, why do you lie asleep? Wake, and weep in fear and sorrow; how can one whose dwelling is (to be) the grave sleep in peace? ॥127॥
1371.6: O Kabir, why do you lie asleep? Why not rise and repeat the Name of Murari (the Lord)? One day you will sleep with your legs stretched out long. ॥128॥
1371.7: O Kabir, why do you lie asleep? Sit up and stay awake; join with the One from whose company you have been parted. ॥129॥
1371.8: O Kabir, one should not leave the way of the Sant; keep walking on that path; at the very sight (of a Sant), one becomes pure, and meeting (him), one repeats the Name. ॥130॥
1371.9: O Kabir, one should not keep the company of a Saakat; let us run far away (from him); touch a blackened vessel, and some stain sticks. ॥131॥
1371.10: O Kabir, (you) did not remember Ram, and old age has arrived; (when fire) has caught the door of the house, what can be brought out now? ॥132॥
1371.11: O Kabir, that came to pass which the Creator did; apart from him there is no other; he alone is the Creator. ॥133॥
1371.12: O Kabir, the trees have begun to bear fruit, and the mangoes have begun to ripen; (they) will reach the owner, if the crows do not eat (them) on the way. ॥134॥
1371.13: O Kabir, (people) buy a Thakur (an idol of the Lord) and worship it, and go to places of pilgrimage out of the mind's stubbornness; copying one another, they put on disguises, and, led astray, wander lost. ॥135॥
1371.14: O Kabir, a stone has been made the Supreme God, and the whole world worships (it); those who rested on this trust have drowned in the black current. ॥136॥
1371.15: O Kabir, (the scriptures of) paper are a cell, and the rituals (written in) ink its doors; the stones have drowned (the people of) the earth, and the pandits have plundered the road. ॥137॥
1371.16: O Kabir, what you would do tomorrow, do today; what you would do today, (do) this very moment; later nothing can be done, when death comes down upon your head. ॥138॥
1371.17: O Kabir, I saw a creature that (shone) like washed lac; he seems clever and full of virtues, (but is) without understanding, and unclean. ॥139॥
1371.18: O Kabir, Jam cannot treat my understanding with contempt; (for I) have repeated the Name of the Cherisher who created this petty Jam. ॥140॥
1371.19: Kabir has become musk, and all the servants (of God) have become bumblebees (drawn to it); the more Kabir's devotion (grows), the more Ram dwells (in him). ॥141॥
1372.1: O Kabir, (man) is caught in the tangle of his family, and Ram is left aside on the bank; (the messengers) of Dharam Raj have fallen (on him) in the midst of all the bustle. ॥142॥
1372.2: O Kabir, better than a Saakat is a pig, (which) keeps the village clean; the wretched Saakat has died, and no one will (ever) speak his name. ॥143॥
1372.3: O Kabir, adding cowrie to cowrie, (man) has gathered hundreds of thousands and tens of millions; (but) at the time of departure he got nothing: even his loincloth was torn off. ॥144॥
1372.4: O Kabir, what of it, if one has become a Vaishnav and put on four rosaries? Outside (he is) pure gold, (but) inside he is filled with rubbish. ॥145॥
1372.5: O Kabir, become a pebble on the path, giving up the pride of your mind; if there is a servant such as this, God meets him. ॥146॥
1372.6: O Kabir, what of it, if one has become a pebble? (It) hurts the traveller; (O Lord,) your servant is such as the dust of the earth. ॥147॥
1372.7: O Kabir, what of it, if one has become dust? (It) flies up and clings to the body; the Lord's servant should be like water, (which washes) every limb. ॥148॥
1372.8: O Kabir, what of it, if one has become water? (It) turns cold and hot; the Lord's servant should be such as the Lord himself is. ॥149॥
1372.9: (Though there be) lofty mansions, gold and a beautiful woman, and a flag fluttering on the pinnacle, better than that is alms begged from door to door, (if, living on it, one) sings the praises (of God) in the company of the Sants. ॥150॥
1372.10: O Kabir, a wilderness is better than a city, (if) it is a place where the devotees of Ram (dwell); (a place) without those who love Ram is the city of Jam in my eyes. ॥151॥
1372.11: O Kabir, between the Ganga and the Jamuna lies the ghat of Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) and Sunn (the stillness where no worldly thought stirs); there Kabir has made his dwelling, the way to which the sages go searching for. ॥152॥
1372.12: O Kabir, if (love) lasts to the end just as it sprang up at the start, then of what account is a poor diamond? Millions of jewels do not come up to (it). ॥153॥
1372.13: O Kabir, I have seen a wonder: a diamond is being sold in the market; with no trader (who knows its worth), it is going for a cowrie shell. ॥154॥
1372.14: O Kabir, where there is wisdom, righteousness is there; where there is falsehood, sin is there; where there is greed, death is there; where there is forgiveness, (God) himself is there. ॥155॥
1372.15: O Kabir, what of it, if one has renounced Maya, when pride cannot be renounced? Through pride, sages and the greatest of sages have wasted away; pride devours everyone. ॥156॥
1372.16: O Kabir, I have met the True Guru, the true one, who loosed a single (arrow) of the Shabad; the moment it struck, I was laid in the dust, and a hole was bored in (my) heart. ॥157॥
1372.17: O Kabir, what can (even) the True Guru, the true one, do, if the fault lies in the disciples? On the blind not one (teaching) takes hold, as when one plays a bamboo by blowing into it (and the breath passes straight through). ॥158॥
1372.18: O Kabir, (there may be) the queen of a sovereign king, (with) horses, elephants and carriages in countless throngs, (yet) she does not come up to the woman who carries water for the Lord's servant. ॥159॥
1373.1: O Kabir, why should the king's queen be reproached? Why should the Lord's maidservant be honoured? The one (the queen) dresses the parting of her hair for sensual pleasure; the other (the maidservant) remembers the Name of the Lord. ॥160॥
1373.2: O Kabir, (when) the prop (of the Name) was found, (the mind) grew steady; the True Guru gave (me) courage; Kabir has traded in the diamond on the shore of Mansarovar. ॥161॥
In Indian poetry the swan lives on the lake Mansarovar and feeds on pearls.
1373.3: O Kabir, the Lord is the diamond, and his servant the jeweller, who takes it and sets out his shop; only when appraisers are found does the trade in diamonds take place. ॥162॥
1373.4: O Kabir, as one remembers the Lord when need befalls, so remember him always; (so) make your home in the deathless city; the Lord brings back the wealth that was lost. ॥163॥
1373.5: O Kabir, two are good to serve: the one the Sant, the other Ram; Ram, who is the giver of liberation, and the Sant, who leads (others) to repeat the Name. ॥164॥
1373.6: O Kabir, on the road the pandits took, the crowd followed behind; there is a steep and difficult pass (that leads) to Ram, and Kabir is climbing it. ॥165॥
1373.7: O Kabir, (the mortal) has died worrying over the world, keeping to the bounds of his family's custom; when they carry him off and lay him in the cremation ground, whose family will then be put to shame? ॥166॥
1373.8: O Kabir, you will drown, poor wretch, in your regard for what many people think; what has befallen your neighbour, know that it will befall you too. ॥167॥
1373.9: O Kabir, good is alms begged from door to door, grain of many kinds; no one holds a claim (on it); (for the beggar) there is a vast country, a vast kingdom. ॥168॥
1373.10: O Kabir, laying claim to things brings burning; the one who makes no claim stays free of care; the one who stays without claims counts even one like Indra a pauper. ॥169॥
1373.11: O Kabir, the pool is full to its banks, yet no one can drink its water; you have found (it) through great good fortune; O Kabir, fill (your cup) again and again, and drink. ॥170॥
1373.12: O Kabir, as the stars fade at dawn, so this body fades away; (but) these two letters (of Ram) do not fade; Kabir holds fast to them. ॥171॥
1373.13: O Kabir, the house is of wood, and fire has caught it on all ten sides; the pandits, wise in their own eyes, have burnt to death; the fools ran off and escaped. ॥172॥
1373.14: O Kabir, cast off (your) doubt; let the papers float away; sift the fifty-two letters (of all learning) to their essence, and fix your mind on the feet of the Lord. ॥173॥
1373.15: O Kabir, the Sant does not give up his saintliness, though he meets millions of the unholy; the sandalwood is wound about with snakes, yet it does not give up its coolness. ॥174॥
1373.16: O Kabir, (my) mind has grown cool, (for I) have gained the knowledge of God; to the servant (of God), the fire that has burnt up the world is like water. ॥175॥
1373.17: O Kabir, no one knows (the play) the Creator has made; either the Master himself knows it, or (his) servant who stays in (his) court. ॥176॥
1373.18: O Kabir, it is well that the fear (of God) came upon (me); all (other) directions were forgotten; the hailstone melted into water, and, flowing down, it went and joined the river. ॥177॥
1374.1: O Kabir, gathering dust together, the body has been built (like) a little town; it is a sight for four days; in the end, it is dust, (back to) dust. ॥178॥
1374.2: O Kabir, with the rising of the sun and the moon, all bodies came into being; (but) without meeting the Guru, Gobind, they all turned back into dust. ॥179॥
1374.3: Where there is inner experience (of God), there are no fears; where there is fear, the Lord is not. Kabir has said this after reflection: hear it in your minds, O Sants. ॥180॥
1374.4: O Kabir, those who have understood nothing pass (their lives) in peaceful sleep; (but) on us, who have understood what was to be understood, the full trouble has fallen. ॥181॥
1374.5: O Kabir, the one who is beaten cries out a great deal; pain cries out in another way; (but when) the blow struck the very core, Kabir stayed still where he was. ॥182॥
1374.6: O Kabir, the blow of a spear is easy to bear; when it strikes, (one) heaves a sigh; (but whoever) bears the blow of the Shabad — he is the Guru, and I am his servant. ॥183॥
1374.7: O Kabir, O mullah, why do you climb the minaret? The Master is not deaf; he for whom you give the call to prayer — look for him within your own heart. ॥184॥
1374.8: O Sheikh, if you are without patience, what is the use of going to the Kaaba on Hajj? O Kabir, one whose heart is not whole — where is God for him? ॥185॥
1374.9: O Kabir, worship Allah, remembering whom suffering departs; the Master becomes manifest in the heart, and the burning (fire) is put out by (his) Name. ॥186॥
1374.10: O Kabir, to do (a thing) by force is oppression, though you call it halal (lawful); when the account is called for in (God's) office, what will (your) state be then? ॥187॥
1374.11: O Kabir, a meal of khichri is fine fare, with salt in it (as sweet as) Amrit; who would have a throat cut for the sake of meat with bread? ॥188॥
1374.12: O Kabir, know that the Guru has taken hold (of one) when attachment and the fevers of the body are ended; (when) joy and grief no longer burn (the mind), then there is the Lord, he himself alone. ॥189॥
1374.13: O Kabir, there is a difference in saying Ram; there is one thing in it to reflect on; all speak that same (name) Ram, and the players in shows (speak) the same. ॥190॥
1374.14: O Kabir, say Ram, Ram alone, (but keep) discernment in the saying; the One (Ram) has blended into the many, (while) one (Ram) was contained in one (body). ॥191॥
1374.15: O Kabir, the homes where the Saadhs are not served, nor is the Lord served, those homes are like cremation grounds; ghosts dwell in them. ॥192॥
1374.16: O Kabir, (I) have become dumb, crazed, deaf in the ears, lame in the feet: the True Guru has struck (me) with his arrow. ॥193॥
1374.17: O Kabir, the one arrow that the True Guru, the warrior, loosed — the moment it struck, I fell to the ground, and a hole was bored in (my) heart. ॥194॥
1374.18: O Kabir, a pure drop from the sky fell on barren ground; without the Sangat, a human being is like this: (the drop) has become the ash of a furnace. ॥195॥
1375.1: O Kabir, the (prepared) ground has taken the pure drop from the sky into itself; countless clever men have worn themselves out, (but) it cannot be separated (from it). ॥196॥
1375.2: O Kabir, I was on my way to the Kaaba for Hajj, and on the road I met God; the Master quarrelled with me (and said): Who ordered you (to sacrifice) a cow? ॥197॥
1375.3: O Kabir, Kabir has gone to the Kaaba on Hajj many a time; O Master, what is my fault, (that my) Pir does not speak (to me) with his own mouth? ॥198॥
1375.4: O Kabir, those who kill living beings by force, and say that it is halal, when God brings out (their) record, what will (their) state be? ॥199॥
1375.5: O Kabir, the force one has used is oppression; God demands an answer for it; (when) the account (against him) comes out of the office, (he) is struck on the face, blow upon blow. ॥200॥
1375.6: O Kabir, rendering the account is easy, if the heart is pure; in that true court, no one seizes (him) by the hem. ॥201॥
1375.7: O Kabir, O duality, in earth and sky you are mighty and cannot be slain; the followers of the six darshanas (the six schools of philosophy) and the eighty-four Siddhas have fallen into doubt (through you). ॥202॥
1375.8: O Kabir, nothing in me is mine; whatever there is, is yours; in handing over to you what is yours, what does it cost me? ॥203॥
1375.9: O Kabir, saying you, you, I have become you; no I is left in me; when (the line between) self and other was erased, wherever I look, there are you. ॥204॥
1375.10: O Kabir, (people) kept brooding on vices and nursing false hopes; not one desire (of theirs) was fulfilled, and they rose and departed in despair. ॥205॥
1375.11: O Kabir, whoever remembers the Lord is at peace in the world; one whom the Creator protects never wavers anywhere, here or hereafter. ॥206॥
1375.12: O Kabir, (we) were being crushed in the oil press; the True Guru set (us) free; the devotion of long ages past came and showed itself. ॥207॥
1375.13: O Kabir, the day (of life) has passed in putting things off, and the interest goes on mounting; the Lord has not been worshipped, the bond (of debt) has not been torn up, and death has arrived. ॥208॥
1375.14: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Kabir, the barking dog gets up and runs after carrion; (but) by (God's) grace I have found the True Guru, who has set me free (from it). ॥209॥
1375.15: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Kabir, the land belongs to the Saadhs, (yet) thieves come in and sit down among (them); the land does not feel (their) weight, and they reap gain upon gain. ॥210॥
1375.16: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Kabir, for the sake of the rice, the husk is beaten with the pestle; (so too,) those who sit in evil company are then questioned by Dharam Raj. ॥211॥
1375.17: Tilochan says: O friend Nama, (you) are bewitched by Maya; why do you print calico? Why do you not fix your mind on Ram? ॥212॥
Namdev was a calico printer by trade; Tilochan was a devotee of his time.
1375.18: Nama says: O Tilochan, keep Ram on your lips; do all your work with your hands and feet, (but keep) your mind with the Immaculate (Lord). ॥213॥
1376.1: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Kabir, no one is ours, and we are no one's; (we) remain absorbed in him who made this creation. ॥214॥
1376.2: O Kabir, the flour fell into the mud, and nothing came to hand; what was chewed while grinding and grinding — that alone stayed with (one). ॥215॥
1376.3: O Kabir, the mind knows all about it, and knowing, still does wrong; what well-being is this, (when one) falls into the well with a lamp in hand? ॥216॥
1376.4: O Kabir, (my) love is fixed on the All-wise (Lord), (but) ignorant people forbid (me); how can it go well, broken off from him to whom (this) soul and breath belong? ॥217॥
1376.5: O Kabir, why do you wear yourselves to death adorning houses and pavilions you are attached to? The need is for three and a half cubits (of ground), or, (if) more, three and three-quarters. ॥218॥
1376.6: O Kabir, what I plan, (the Lord) does not do; what can come of my planning? The Lord does what he himself has planned, which is not (even) in my mind. ॥219॥
1376.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). (God) himself brings on anxiety, and himself grants freedom from care; O Nanak, let us praise him who takes care of all. ॥220॥
1376.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O Kabir, (the mortal) did not remember Ram, and wandered about in greed; committing sins, he died; his span of life ran out in an instant. ॥221॥
1376.9: O Kabir, the body is an unbaked pitcher, made of nothing but raw clay; if you would keep it whole, worship Ram; otherwise the matter is lost. ॥222॥
1376.10: O Kabir, let us keep calling Keshav, Keshav, and not sleep heedless; calling out night and day, some day or other (he) will hear the cry. ॥223॥
1376.11: O Kabir, the body has become Kajli Ban (a dense forest), and the mind (in it) an elephant crazed with rut; the jewel of (divine) knowledge is the goad, and the one who drives it is a rare Sant. ॥224॥
1376.12: O Kabir, (the Name of) Ram is the jewel, the mouth its purse; open (the purse) before one who can appraise it; some customer will come along, who will buy it at a high price. ॥225॥
1376.13: O Kabir, (the mortal) did not know the Name of Ram, (but) reared a household as big as an army; he died in his worldly affairs and nothing else, and not a sound (of him) came out beyond them. ॥226॥
1376.14: O Kabir, in blinks of the eyes, moment by moment, (life) has slipped away; (yet) the mind does not let go of its entanglements; Jam has come and beaten the drum. ॥227॥
1376.15: O Kabir, Ram is (like) a tree, detachment its fruit; the Saadh, who has given up wrangling and dispute, is its shade. ॥228॥
1376.16: O Kabir, sow such a seed as bears fruit all twelve months, with cool shade and fruit in plenty, and birds sporting (in its branches). ॥229॥
1376.17: O Kabir, the giver is (like) a tree, compassion its fruit; he lives doing good to others; the birds fly away to other lands, (yet) the tree goes on bearing good fruit. ॥230॥
1376.18: O Kabir, the company of the Saadh is gained (when it) is written on the forehead; (through it) the gift of liberation is gained, and on the hard pass there is no barrier. ॥231॥
1377.1: O Kabir, one ghari (a measure of about twenty-four minutes), half a ghari, (or) half of the half — whatever converse is held with the devotees, that is the gain. ॥232॥
1377.2: O Kabir, all the mortals who take hemp, fish and wine, the pilgrimages, fasts and observances (they) have kept — all of these go down to Rasatal (the nether world). ॥233॥
1377.3: I keep my eyes lowered, holding the Friend within my heart; I take every delight with my Beloved, and let no one see it. ॥234॥
1377.4: All eight watches (of day and night), all sixty-four gharis, my soul goes on gazing at you; why should I lower my eyes? In every body I see the Beloved. ॥235॥
1377.5: Listen, my friend: does the soul dwell in the Beloved, or does the Beloved dwell in the soul? I cannot tell soul and Beloved apart: is it the soul in the body, or the Beloved? ॥236॥
1377.6: O Kabir, the Brahmin is guru to the world, (but) to the devotees he is no guru; tangled and entangled in the four Vedas, he has worn himself out to death. ॥237॥
1377.7: The Lord is sugar scattered in the sand; an elephant cannot pick it up; says Kabir, the Guru has made (this) well understood: it is by becoming an ant that one eats it. ॥238॥
1377.8: O Kabir, if you long for (the game of) love, cut off your head and make it a ball; playing on and on, lose yourself in ecstasy; then let come what may. ॥239॥
1377.9: O Kabir, if you long for (the game of) love, play with one who is ripe; unripe mustard, crushed, has yielded neither oilcake nor oil. ॥240॥
1377.10: Searching, (people) stumble about like the blind, and do not recognise the Sants; says Nama, how can God be found without the devotees? ॥241॥
1377.11: Those who leave a diamond such as the Lord and set their hopes on another, those men will go to hell: Ravidas speaks the truth. ॥242॥
1377.12: O Kabir, if you keep a household, practise righteousness; if not, take up renunciation; (if) a renunciant (then) takes on bonds, great is his misfortune. ॥243॥

1364.10: The saloks of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O Kabir, my rosary is (my) tongue, on which is (the Name of) Ram.
From the beginning, from the start of the ages, he has been the peace and resting place of all the devotees. ॥1॥
1364.11: O Kabir, everyone laughs at my caste;
(but) I am a sacrifice to this caste, in which (born, I) have repeated the Name of the Creator. ॥2॥
1364.12: O Kabir, why do you waver? Why do you let your soul be shaken?
Drink the sweet essence of the Name of Ram, the master of all comforts. ॥3॥
1364.13: O Kabir, (if) earrings are made of gold, with rubies set in them,
(still, on) those in whose mind the Name is not, (the earrings) look like burnt reeds. ॥4॥
1364.14: O Kabir, rare is such a one, hardly one or two, who is dead while yet alive,
and, become fearless, sings the praises (of God); wherever I look, there he is. ॥5॥
1364.15: O Kabir, the day I died (to self), after that came bliss;
I met my God, and (now my) companions (too) worship Gobind. ॥6॥
1364.16: O Kabir, I am the worst of all; everyone but me is good.
Whoever has come to understand (himself) so is my friend. ॥7॥
1364.17: O Kabir, (Maya, the world's illusion and lure,) came to me in many guises;
(but) my Guru saved me, and she bowed (to me). ॥8॥
1364.18: O Kabir, let us kill only that (Haumai, ego) whose death brings peace;
everyone calls (its killing) good, good; no one takes (it) as bad. ॥9॥
1364.19: O Kabir, the nights are dark, and the black-(hearted) creatures rise up;
taking nooses, they rise and run out; know that they are struck down by God. ॥10॥
1365.1: O Kabir, (even) a small sandalwood plant is good, (though) it is hemmed in by dhaak and palaas trees;
they too, who dwell near the sandalwood, become sandalwood. ॥11॥
1365.2: O Kabir, the bamboo is drowned in (the pride of) its greatness; let no one drown like this.
The bamboo dwells near the sandalwood, (yet) it does not become fragrant. ॥12॥
1365.3: O Kabir, (man) lost his deen (the way of God) for the sake of the world, (but) the world did not go with (him).
The heedless one struck his own foot with an axe, by his own hand. ॥13॥
1365.4: O Kabir, wherever I have wandered, (I saw) spectacles in place after place;
(but) without one who loves Ram, (it is all) a wilderness in my eyes. ॥14॥
1365.5: O Kabir, the hut of the Sants is good; the village of the false is a furnace.
Let fire take that mansion in which there is not the Name of the Lord. ॥15॥
1365.6: O Kabir, why weep when a Sant dies? He goes to his own home.
Weep for the wretched Saakat (one who has turned from God), who is sold from shop to shop. ॥16॥
1365.7: O Kabir, the Saakat is like a store of garlic;
eat it sitting in a corner, (yet) in the end it becomes known. ॥17॥
1365.8: O Kabir, Maya is the churning pot, and the breath is the churner;
the Sants have eaten the butter, (while) the world drinks the buttermilk. ॥18॥
1365.9: O Kabir, Maya is the churning pot, and the breath flows like a cool stream;
the one who churned has eaten (the butter); the others are (only) churning. ॥19॥
1365.10: O Kabir, Maya is a thief, who robs and robs (people) and stocks (her) shop;
Kabir alone is not robbed (by her), for he has cut her into twelve pieces. ॥20॥
1365.11: O Kabir, in this world there is no peace (for those) who make many friends;
those who keep their mind on the One find peace always. ॥21॥
1365.12: O Kabir, the death the world fears (brings) joy to my mind;
only by dying is the perfect, supreme Bliss (God) found. ॥22॥
1365.13: Having found the treasure of Ram, O Kabir, do not untie its bundle;
(for it) there is no market, no assayer, no buyer, no price. ॥23॥
1365.14: O Kabir, love the one whose Master is Ram;
pandits, kings and lords of the land, of what use are they? ॥24॥
1365.15: O Kabir, by loving the One, every other duality goes;
whether you grow your hair long, or shave (your head) bare. ॥25॥
1365.16: O Kabir, the world is a chamber of soot; the blind have fallen into it.
I am a sacrifice to those who, having entered, come out (again). ॥26॥
1365.17: O Kabir, this body will go; if you can, turn it back.
Those who had hundreds of thousands and tens of millions departed barefoot. ॥27॥
1365.18: O Kabir, this body will go; set it on some (good) path:
either keep the company of the Saadh (the holy one), or sing the praises of the Lord. ॥28॥
1365.19: O Kabir, dying and dying, the whole world has died, yet no one has known even how to die.
One who dies such a death will not die again. ॥29॥
1366.1: O Kabir, human birth is hard to obtain; it does not come again and again;
as the fruits of the forest, once ripe, fall to the ground and are not joined to the branch again. ॥30॥
1366.2: O Kabir, (say, O Lord,) you alone are Kabir (the Great); your Name is Kabir.
The jewel of Ram is found only when (you) first give up (attachment to) the body. ॥31॥
1366.3: O Kabir, let us not fret and complain; nothing comes of what you say.
The favours that Kareem (the Gracious Lord) bestows, no one can erase. ॥32॥
1366.4: O Kabir, (on) the touchstone of Ram no false one can stand.
The touchstone of Ram is borne only by one who has died and come alive. ॥33॥
1366.5: O Kabir, (people) wear white clothes and chew betel and areca nut;
(but) without the Name of the one Lord, they go bound to the city of Jam (the messenger of Death). ॥34॥
1366.6: O Kabir, the boat is rotten, with thousands of holes burst open;
the light ones have floated across; those with loads on their heads have drowned. ॥35॥
1366.7: O Kabir, the bones burn as wood does, and the hair as grass;
seeing this world burning, Kabir has grown detached. ॥36॥
1366.8: O Kabir, one should not be proud: (the body is but) bones wrapped in skin.
Those (who rode) on fine horses, under royal canopies, were at last buried in the earth too. ॥37॥
1366.9: O Kabir, one should not be proud, seeing one's lofty house;
today or tomorrow (you) will lie on the ground, and grass will grow over (you). ॥38॥
1366.10: O Kabir, one should not be proud, nor laugh at anyone poor;
(your) boat is still out at sea: what do I know of what may happen? ॥39॥
1366.11: O Kabir, one should not be proud, seeing one's fair body;
today or tomorrow (you) will leave it behind, as a snake its slough. ॥40॥
1366.12: O Kabir, if you would plunder, plunder now: the Name of Ram is there to be plundered;
or else you will repent later, (when) the breath of life slips away. ॥41॥
1366.13: O Kabir, no one has been born such as would set fire to his own house,
and, burning the five sons, remain lovingly attuned to Ram. ॥42॥
1366.14: Is there anyone who would sell (his) son, and sell (his) daughter,
go into partnership with Kabir, and trade with the Lord? ॥43॥
1366.15: O Kabir, (I give you) this warning, lest any doubt remain (in your mind):
for the pleasures (you) have enjoyed till now, take (a little) molasses in exchange and eat it. ॥44॥
1366.16: O Kabir, I had thought that reading was good; (but) better than reading is union (with God);
I will not give up devotion to Ram, even if people slander (me). ॥45॥
1366.17: O Kabir, why should the poor people slander, who have no wisdom in their mind?
Kabir is absorbed in Ram, and has given up all other work. ॥46॥
1366.18: O Kabir, on all four sides fire has caught the robe of the stranger (soul);
the patched coat (of the body) has burnt to charcoal, but the thread (of the soul) was not touched by the flame. ॥47॥
1366.19: O Kabir, the patched coat has burnt to charcoal, and the begging bowl is smashed to pieces;
the wretched yogi's play is over; only ashes are left on his seat. ॥48॥
1367.1: O Kabir, the fish is in shallow water, and the fisherman has cast his net;
(O fish,) in this little pool you will not escape; turn back and make for the ocean. ॥49॥
1367.2: O Kabir, one should not forsake the ocean, even if its water is very salty;
no one will call good one who searches from pond to pond. ॥50॥
1367.3: O Kabir, those without a master (without a Guru) are swept away; there is no one to hold them.
(Those who) have made meekness and humility their own (accept that) what comes from the Creator comes. ॥51॥
1367.4: O Kabir, the dog of a Vaishnav (the true devotee) is good, the mother of a Saakat is bad;
the one hears the praise of the Lord's Name every day, (while) the other goes out to buy sin. ॥52॥
1367.5: O Kabir, the deer is weak, and this pool is lush and green;
the hunters are a hundred thousand, the life one: how long can I escape death? ॥53॥
1367.6: O Kabir, (those) who make their home on the bank of the Ganga, and drink its pure water,
without devotion to the Lord (even they) are not liberated; so saying, Kabir dwells on Ram. ॥54॥
1367.7: O Kabir, (my) mind has become pure, like the water of the Ganga;
(now) the Lord follows behind (me), calling, Kabir, Kabir. ॥55॥
1367.8: O Kabir, turmeric is yellow, and lime is white in hue;
the lover of Ram meets (Ram) only when both colours (both castes) are lost. ॥56॥
1367.9: O Kabir, turmeric loses its yellowness, and no trace of the lime's white remains;
I am a sacrifice to this love, through which caste, colour and lineage depart. ॥57॥
1367.10: O Kabir, the door of liberation is narrow, a tenth part of a mustard seed;
but the mind has become a maddened elephant: how can it pass through? ॥58॥
1367.11: O Kabir, if such a True Guru is met, who, well pleased, shows his grace,
then the door of liberation is wide, and I come and go (through it) with ease. ॥59॥
1367.12: O Kabir, I have no thatch and no hut, I have no house and no village;
perhaps the Lord will ask who this is; I have neither caste nor name. ॥60॥
1367.13: O Kabir, I long to die; and if I die, (let it be) at the Lord's door;
perhaps the Lord will ask who this is, lying at my door. ॥61॥
1367.14: O Kabir, I have not done (anything), nor shall I do, nor can (this) body do (anything);
what do I know? Whatever (was done), the Lord did, and Kabir became Kabir. ॥62॥
1367.15: O Kabir, one from whose mouth Ram comes forth, even when babbling in a dream,
(let) the shoes on his feet (be made) of the skin of my body. ॥63॥
1367.16: O Kabir, we are puppets of clay, (yet we) have given (ourselves) the name of man;
(we are) guests for four days, (yet) we take up great, great places. ॥64॥
1367.17: O Kabir, making myself henna, I toiled, having myself ground and ground (fine);
(but) you, O Husband Lord, did not ask after (me), and never put (me) to your feet. ॥65॥
1367.18: O Kabir, the door where no one stops (us), coming or going,
how can one leave a door that is such? ॥66॥
1367.19: O Kabir, I was drowning, but was saved, lifted in a flash by a wave of (God's) virtues;
when I saw that the boat was rotten, I leapt and got off (it). ॥67॥
1368.1: O Kabir, devotion does not please the sinner, nor does the worship of the Lord appeal to him;
the fly forsakes the sandalwood, and goes where there is a stench. ॥68॥
1368.2: O Kabir, the physician has died, the patient has died, the whole world has died;
Kabir alone has not died, for whom there is no one to weep. ॥69॥
1368.3: O Kabir, Ram was not meditated on, (and so) a heavy rot has set in;
the body is a wooden pot: it cannot be set (on the fire) again. ॥70॥
1368.4: O Kabir, it has come about that (I) have done what my mind loved;
why fear death, once (the sati) has taken the vermilion-smeared coconut in her hand? ॥71॥
1368.5: O Kabir, the cane is sucked for its juice; for virtues one must weep and die.
No one will call good a man full of faults. ॥72॥
1368.6: O Kabir, the pitcher is full of water; today or tomorrow (it) will break.
Those who do not remember their Guru will be robbed halfway (on the road). ॥73॥
1368.7: O Kabir, I am the dog of Ram; Moti is my name;
around my neck is a rope: wherever (he) pulls, there (I) go. ॥74॥
1368.8: O Kabir, why do you show the world your rosary of wood?
(If) you do not remember Ram in your heart, what use is this rosary? ॥75॥
1368.9: O Kabir, (in whose) mind the serpent of separation dwells, on (him) no charm works;
one parted from Ram does not live; and if he lives, he goes mad. ॥76॥
1368.10: O Kabir, the paaras and the sandalwood have one quality in common:
meeting them, even iron and scentless wood become excellent. ॥77॥
1368.11: O Kabir, the club of Jam is terrible: it cannot be endured;
(but) I met a Saadh, and he took me to the hem (of his robe). ॥78॥
1368.12: O Kabir, the physician says: I alone am good; the cure is in my hands;
(but) this (life) is the property of Gopal (the sustainer of the world): when it pleases (him), (he) takes it back. ॥79॥
1368.13: O Kabir, beat your own drum for ten days;
like the meeting (of passengers) in a river boat, (this meeting) will not come again. ॥80॥
1368.14: O Kabir, if I make the seven seas ink, and make all the plants pens,
and make the earth paper, (still) the praise of the Lord cannot be written. ॥81॥
1368.15: O Kabir, what (harm) can (my) caste, the weaver's, do, (when) Gopal dwells in (my) heart?
O Kabir, meet the all-pervading Lord in his embrace, and all entanglements will end. ॥82॥
1368.16: O Kabir, there is no one such as would burn down (his) house,
and, killing the five sons, remain lovingly attuned to Ram. ॥83॥
1368.17: O Kabir, there is no one such as would set fire to (his attachment to) this body;
the blind world does not understand, (though) Kabir keeps crying it aloud. ॥84॥
1368.18: O Kabir, the sati, mounted on the pyre, cries out: Listen, O brother cremation ground:
all the people have gone away; in the end it is you and I who have business together. ॥85॥
1369.1: O Kabir, the mind has become a bird; it flies and flies off in the ten directions;
whatever company one finds, such is the fruit one eats. ॥86॥
1369.2: O Kabir, the place I was searching for, that very place I have found;
you have turned and become the very One whom you used to call another. ॥87॥
1369.3: O Kabir, I am dying, struck down by bad company, like a banana plant that stands near a jujube tree;
the one (the jujube) sways, and the other (the banana) is torn; do not look toward the company of a Saakat. ॥88॥
1369.4: O Kabir, others' load keeps mounting on (a man's) head, and (still) he wants to walk the road;
he does not fear his own load, (though) ahead lies a hard and treacherous pass. ॥89॥
1369.5: O Kabir, the burnt wood of the forest stands and cries out:
may I not fall into the blacksmith's hands, (for he) will burn (me) a second time. ॥90॥
1369.6: O Kabir, when one died, two died; when two died, four;
when four died, six died: four males and two females. ॥91॥
1369.7: O Kabir, I searched the world, looking and looking, (but) nowhere found a place (of rest);
those who have not remembered the Name of the Lord, why do they stray off elsewhere? ॥92॥
1369.8: O Kabir, let us keep the company of the Saadh, (which) stands by us to the end;
one should not keep the company of a Saakat, from which comes ruin. ॥93॥
1369.9: O Kabir, (those who) in this world remembered (God), knowing that he pervades the world, (have made their birth fruitful);
those who have not remembered the Name of the Lord were born in vain. ॥94॥
1369.10: O Kabir, let us place our hope in Ram; hope in others (ends) in despair.
Those men who turn away from the Name of the Lord fall into hell. ॥95॥
1369.11: O Kabir, (they) made many disciples and followers, (but) did not make Keshav (the Lord) their friend;
(they) had set out to meet the Lord, (but their) mind got stuck on the way. ॥96॥
1369.12: O Kabir, what can the poor creature do, if Ram (himself) gives no help?
Whatever branch I set my foot on bends and bends (and breaks). ॥97॥
1369.13: O Kabir, those who preach to others, sand falls into (their own) mouths;
they guard the wealth of others, (while) the field of their own home has been eaten up. ॥98॥
1369.14: O Kabir, (let me) stay in the company of the Saadh, (even if I) eat barley husks;
what is to be will be; (but let me) not go in the company of Saakats. ॥99॥
1369.15: O Kabir, in the company of the Saadh, love doubles day by day;
the Saakat is a black blanket, which does not become white though it is washed. ॥100॥
1369.16: O Kabir, you have not shaved your mind; why have you had your hair shaved off?
Whatever was done, the mind did; shaving the head is useless. ॥101॥
1369.17: O Kabir, one should not forsake Ram; (if) body and wealth go, let them go;
(my) mind is pierced by the lotus feet (of the Lord); (let me) remain merged in the Name of Ram. ॥102॥
1369.18: O Kabir, the instrument I used to play, all its strings have snapped;
what can the poor instrument do? The player has departed. ॥103॥
1369.19: O Kabir, I would shave the head of the mother of that guru by whom doubt is not dispelled;
(such gurus) are drowned themselves in the four Vedas, and have swept away (their) disciples (too). ॥104॥
1370.1: O Kabir, whatever sins were committed were kept hidden beneath;
(but) in the end they all came to light when Dharam Raj (the judge of souls) asked. ॥105॥
1370.2: O Kabir, giving up the remembrance of the Lord, (man) raised a large family;
busy with his affairs, he passed away, and neither brother nor kinsman remained. ॥106॥
1370.3: O Kabir, (the woman) who, giving up the remembrance of the Lord, goes at night to rouse (the spirits of the cremation ground)
is born a she-serpent, and eats her own offspring. ॥107॥
1370.4: O Kabir, the woman who, giving up the remembrance of the Lord, keeps the fast of Ahoi (the goddess Sitala)
is born a she-donkey, and bears a load of four maunds. ॥108॥
1370.5: O Kabir, the very greatest wisdom is (this): repeat the Name of the Lord within your heart;
(but this) is play on top of a stake: if (one) falls, there is no resting place. ॥109॥
1370.6: O Kabir, blessed is that mouth with which Ram is uttered;
what to say of the poor body? The whole village will be made pure. ॥110॥
1370.7: O Kabir, good is that family in which (is born) a servant of the Lord;
the family in which no servant (of the Lord) is born is (like) the dhaak and palaas trees. ॥111॥
1370.8: O Kabir, (though there be) horses, elephants and carriages in countless throngs, (and) a hundred thousand banners flying,
better than this comfort is begging, if (one's) days pass in remembering the Lord. ॥112॥
1370.9: O Kabir, I have wandered the whole world, with a drum slung on my shoulder;
no one belongs to anyone: I have seen all, tapping and sounding them out. ॥113॥
1370.10: Pearls lie scattered on the path, and a blind man has come along;
without the light of Jagdish (the Lord of the world), the world passes over (them). ॥114॥
1370.11: The line of Kabir is drowned, (now that) the son Kamal is born:
giving up the remembrance of the Lord, (he) has brought wealth home. ॥115॥
1370.12: O Kabir, when you go to meet the Saadh, take no one with you;
do not set your foot back; whatever comes ahead, let it come. ॥116॥
1370.13: O Kabir, with the rope by which the world is bound, do not be bound, O Kabir;
(or) your body, like gold, will be lost, as salt in flour. ॥117॥
1370.14: O Kabir, the swan (the soul) is about to fly, the body about to be buried, (yet the mortal) gives instructions by signs;
even now the creature does not give up the greed of its eyes. ॥118॥
1370.15: O Kabir, (say, O Lord,) let me behold you with my eyes, and hear your Name with my ears;
let me utter your Name with my tongue, and (keep your) lotus feet in my heart. ॥119॥
1370.16: O Kabir, by the grace of the True Guru, I have been spared both heaven and hell;
(now,) from the beginning to the end, I dwell in the joy of the lotus feet (of the Lord). ॥120॥
1370.17: O Kabir, how can the joy of the lotus feet be told or measured?
(Its) glory does not lie in the telling; it is believed only when it is seen. ॥121॥
1370.18: O Kabir, having seen (him), to whom shall I tell it? No one believes what is told.
The Lord is as he is, he alone; (let me) dwell in joy, singing (his) praises. ॥122॥
1371.1: O Kabir, (the kunj, the demoiselle crane,) pecks her feed and remembers (her young), pecks again, and, pecking and pecking, remembers (them);
as the kunj (keeps) her young (in mind), so, O brother, the mind (holds) its attachment to Maya. ॥123॥
1371.2: O Kabir, the sky is overcast with cloud, and its rain has filled the ponds and lakes;
(those) who (still) go thirsting like the chatrik (rain-bird), what will be their state? ॥124॥
1371.3: O Kabir, if the chakvi (the ruddy sheldrake) is parted (from her mate) at night, she comes and meets (him) at dawn;
(but) those who are parted from Ram meet (him) neither by day nor by night. ॥125॥
1371.4: O Kabir, O conch, parted from Ratnakar (the ocean, the mine of jewels), stay in the ocean;
(or else) at every sunrise you will wail in temple after temple. ॥126॥
1371.5: O Kabir, why do you lie asleep? Wake, and weep in fear and sorrow;
how can one whose dwelling is (to be) the grave sleep in peace? ॥127॥
1371.6: O Kabir, why do you lie asleep? Why not rise and repeat the Name of Murari (the Lord)?
One day you will sleep with your legs stretched out long. ॥128॥
1371.7: O Kabir, why do you lie asleep? Sit up and stay awake;
join with the One from whose company you have been parted. ॥129॥
1371.8: O Kabir, one should not leave the way of the Sant; keep walking on that path;
at the very sight (of a Sant), one becomes pure, and meeting (him), one repeats the Name. ॥130॥
1371.9: O Kabir, one should not keep the company of a Saakat; let us run far away (from him);
touch a blackened vessel, and some stain sticks. ॥131॥
1371.10: O Kabir, (you) did not remember Ram, and old age has arrived;
(when fire) has caught the door of the house, what can be brought out now? ॥132॥
1371.11: O Kabir, that came to pass which the Creator did;
apart from him there is no other; he alone is the Creator. ॥133॥
1371.12: O Kabir, the trees have begun to bear fruit, and the mangoes have begun to ripen;
(they) will reach the owner, if the crows do not eat (them) on the way. ॥134॥
1371.13: O Kabir, (people) buy a Thakur (an idol of the Lord) and worship it, and go to places of pilgrimage out of the mind's stubbornness;
copying one another, they put on disguises, and, led astray, wander lost. ॥135॥
1371.14: O Kabir, a stone has been made the Supreme God, and the whole world worships (it);
those who rested on this trust have drowned in the black current. ॥136॥
1371.15: O Kabir, (the scriptures of) paper are a cell, and the rituals (written in) ink its doors;
the stones have drowned (the people of) the earth, and the pandits have plundered the road. ॥137॥
1371.16: O Kabir, what you would do tomorrow, do today; what you would do today, (do) this very moment;
later nothing can be done, when death comes down upon your head. ॥138॥
1371.17: O Kabir, I saw a creature that (shone) like washed lac;
he seems clever and full of virtues, (but is) without understanding, and unclean. ॥139॥
1371.18: O Kabir, Jam cannot treat my understanding with contempt;
(for I) have repeated the Name of the Cherisher who created this petty Jam. ॥140॥
1371.19: Kabir has become musk, and all the servants (of God) have become bumblebees (drawn to it);
the more Kabir's devotion (grows), the more Ram dwells (in him). ॥141॥
1372.1: O Kabir, (man) is caught in the tangle of his family, and Ram is left aside on the bank;
(the messengers) of Dharam Raj have fallen (on him) in the midst of all the bustle. ॥142॥
1372.2: O Kabir, better than a Saakat is a pig, (which) keeps the village clean;
the wretched Saakat has died, and no one will (ever) speak his name. ॥143॥
1372.3: O Kabir, adding cowrie to cowrie, (man) has gathered hundreds of thousands and tens of millions;
(but) at the time of departure he got nothing: even his loincloth was torn off. ॥144॥
1372.4: O Kabir, what of it, if one has become a Vaishnav and put on four rosaries?
Outside (he is) pure gold, (but) inside he is filled with rubbish. ॥145॥
1372.5: O Kabir, become a pebble on the path, giving up the pride of your mind;
if there is a servant such as this, God meets him. ॥146॥
1372.6: O Kabir, what of it, if one has become a pebble? (It) hurts the traveller;
(O Lord,) your servant is such as the dust of the earth. ॥147॥
1372.7: O Kabir, what of it, if one has become dust? (It) flies up and clings to the body;
the Lord's servant should be like water, (which washes) every limb. ॥148॥
1372.8: O Kabir, what of it, if one has become water? (It) turns cold and hot;
the Lord's servant should be such as the Lord himself is. ॥149॥
1372.9: (Though there be) lofty mansions, gold and a beautiful woman, and a flag fluttering on the pinnacle,
better than that is alms begged from door to door, (if, living on it, one) sings the praises (of God) in the company of the Sants. ॥150॥
1372.10: O Kabir, a wilderness is better than a city, (if) it is a place where the devotees of Ram (dwell);
(a place) without those who love Ram is the city of Jam in my eyes. ॥151॥
1372.11: O Kabir, between the Ganga and the Jamuna lies the ghat of Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise) and Sunn (the stillness where no worldly thought stirs);
there Kabir has made his dwelling, the way to which the sages go searching for. ॥152॥
1372.12: O Kabir, if (love) lasts to the end just as it sprang up at the start,
then of what account is a poor diamond? Millions of jewels do not come up to (it). ॥153॥
1372.13: O Kabir, I have seen a wonder: a diamond is being sold in the market;
with no trader (who knows its worth), it is going for a cowrie shell. ॥154॥
1372.14: O Kabir, where there is wisdom, righteousness is there; where there is falsehood, sin is there;
where there is greed, death is there; where there is forgiveness, (God) himself is there. ॥155॥
1372.15: O Kabir, what of it, if one has renounced Maya, when pride cannot be renounced?
Through pride, sages and the greatest of sages have wasted away; pride devours everyone. ॥156॥
1372.16: O Kabir, I have met the True Guru, the true one, who loosed a single (arrow) of the Shabad;
the moment it struck, I was laid in the dust, and a hole was bored in (my) heart. ॥157॥
1372.17: O Kabir, what can (even) the True Guru, the true one, do, if the fault lies in the disciples?
On the blind not one (teaching) takes hold, as when one plays a bamboo by blowing into it (and the breath passes straight through). ॥158॥
1372.18: O Kabir, (there may be) the queen of a sovereign king, (with) horses, elephants and carriages in countless throngs,
(yet) she does not come up to the woman who carries water for the Lord's servant. ॥159॥
1373.1: O Kabir, why should the king's queen be reproached? Why should the Lord's maidservant be honoured?
The one (the queen) dresses the parting of her hair for sensual pleasure; the other (the maidservant) remembers the Name of the Lord. ॥160॥
1373.2: O Kabir, (when) the prop (of the Name) was found, (the mind) grew steady; the True Guru gave (me) courage;
Kabir has traded in the diamond on the shore of Mansarovar. ॥161॥
1373.3: O Kabir, the Lord is the diamond, and his servant the jeweller, who takes it and sets out his shop;
only when appraisers are found does the trade in diamonds take place. ॥162॥
1373.4: O Kabir, as one remembers the Lord when need befalls, so remember him always;
(so) make your home in the deathless city; the Lord brings back the wealth that was lost. ॥163॥
1373.5: O Kabir, two are good to serve: the one the Sant, the other Ram;
Ram, who is the giver of liberation, and the Sant, who leads (others) to repeat the Name. ॥164॥
1373.6: O Kabir, on the road the pandits took, the crowd followed behind;
there is a steep and difficult pass (that leads) to Ram, and Kabir is climbing it. ॥165॥
1373.7: O Kabir, (the mortal) has died worrying over the world, keeping to the bounds of his family's custom;
when they carry him off and lay him in the cremation ground, whose family will then be put to shame? ॥166॥
1373.8: O Kabir, you will drown, poor wretch, in your regard for what many people think;
what has befallen your neighbour, know that it will befall you too. ॥167॥
1373.9: O Kabir, good is alms begged from door to door, grain of many kinds;
no one holds a claim (on it); (for the beggar) there is a vast country, a vast kingdom. ॥168॥
1373.10: O Kabir, laying claim to things brings burning; the one who makes no claim stays free of care;
the one who stays without claims counts even one like Indra a pauper. ॥169॥
1373.11: O Kabir, the pool is full to its banks, yet no one can drink its water;
you have found (it) through great good fortune; O Kabir, fill (your cup) again and again, and drink. ॥170॥
1373.12: O Kabir, as the stars fade at dawn, so this body fades away;
(but) these two letters (of Ram) do not fade; Kabir holds fast to them. ॥171॥
1373.13: O Kabir, the house is of wood, and fire has caught it on all ten sides;
the pandits, wise in their own eyes, have burnt to death; the fools ran off and escaped. ॥172॥
1373.14: O Kabir, cast off (your) doubt; let the papers float away;
sift the fifty-two letters (of all learning) to their essence, and fix your mind on the feet of the Lord. ॥173॥
1373.15: O Kabir, the Sant does not give up his saintliness, though he meets millions of the unholy;
the sandalwood is wound about with snakes, yet it does not give up its coolness. ॥174॥
1373.16: O Kabir, (my) mind has grown cool, (for I) have gained the knowledge of God;
to the servant (of God), the fire that has burnt up the world is like water. ॥175॥
1373.17: O Kabir, no one knows (the play) the Creator has made;
either the Master himself knows it, or (his) servant who stays in (his) court. ॥176॥
1373.18: O Kabir, it is well that the fear (of God) came upon (me); all (other) directions were forgotten;
the hailstone melted into water, and, flowing down, it went and joined the river. ॥177॥
1374.1: O Kabir, gathering dust together, the body has been built (like) a little town;
it is a sight for four days; in the end, it is dust, (back to) dust. ॥178॥
1374.2: O Kabir, with the rising of the sun and the moon, all bodies came into being;
(but) without meeting the Guru, Gobind, they all turned back into dust. ॥179॥
1374.3: Where there is inner experience (of God), there are no fears; where there is fear, the Lord is not.
Kabir has said this after reflection: hear it in your minds, O Sants. ॥180॥
1374.4: O Kabir, those who have understood nothing pass (their lives) in peaceful sleep;
(but) on us, who have understood what was to be understood, the full trouble has fallen. ॥181॥
1374.5: O Kabir, the one who is beaten cries out a great deal; pain cries out in another way;
(but when) the blow struck the very core, Kabir stayed still where he was. ॥182॥
1374.6: O Kabir, the blow of a spear is easy to bear; when it strikes, (one) heaves a sigh;
(but whoever) bears the blow of the Shabad — he is the Guru, and I am his servant. ॥183॥
1374.7: O Kabir, O mullah, why do you climb the minaret? The Master is not deaf;
he for whom you give the call to prayer — look for him within your own heart. ॥184॥
1374.8: O Sheikh, if you are without patience, what is the use of going to the Kaaba on Hajj?
O Kabir, one whose heart is not whole — where is God for him? ॥185॥
1374.9: O Kabir, worship Allah, remembering whom suffering departs;
the Master becomes manifest in the heart, and the burning (fire) is put out by (his) Name. ॥186॥
1374.10: O Kabir, to do (a thing) by force is oppression, though you call it halal (lawful);
when the account is called for in (God's) office, what will (your) state be then? ॥187॥
1374.11: O Kabir, a meal of khichri is fine fare, with salt in it (as sweet as) Amrit;
who would have a throat cut for the sake of meat with bread? ॥188॥
1374.12: O Kabir, know that the Guru has taken hold (of one) when attachment and the fevers of the body are ended;
(when) joy and grief no longer burn (the mind), then there is the Lord, he himself alone. ॥189॥
1374.13: O Kabir, there is a difference in saying Ram; there is one thing in it to reflect on;
all speak that same (name) Ram, and the players in shows (speak) the same. ॥190॥
1374.14: O Kabir, say Ram, Ram alone, (but keep) discernment in the saying;
the One (Ram) has blended into the many, (while) one (Ram) was contained in one (body). ॥191॥
1374.15: O Kabir, the homes where the Saadhs are not served, nor is the Lord served,
those homes are like cremation grounds; ghosts dwell in them. ॥192॥
1374.16: O Kabir, (I) have become dumb, crazed, deaf in the ears,
lame in the feet: the True Guru has struck (me) with his arrow. ॥193॥
1374.17: O Kabir, the one arrow that the True Guru, the warrior, loosed —
the moment it struck, I fell to the ground, and a hole was bored in (my) heart. ॥194॥
1374.18: O Kabir, a pure drop from the sky fell on barren ground;
without the Sangat, a human being is like this: (the drop) has become the ash of a furnace. ॥195॥
1375.1: O Kabir, the (prepared) ground has taken the pure drop from the sky into itself;
countless clever men have worn themselves out, (but) it cannot be separated (from it). ॥196॥
1375.2: O Kabir, I was on my way to the Kaaba for Hajj, and on the road I met God;
the Master quarrelled with me (and said): Who ordered you (to sacrifice) a cow? ॥197॥
1375.3: O Kabir, Kabir has gone to the Kaaba on Hajj many a time;
O Master, what is my fault, (that my) Pir does not speak (to me) with his own mouth? ॥198॥
1375.4: O Kabir, those who kill living beings by force, and say that it is halal,
when God brings out (their) record, what will (their) state be? ॥199॥
1375.5: O Kabir, the force one has used is oppression; God demands an answer for it;
(when) the account (against him) comes out of the office, (he) is struck on the face, blow upon blow. ॥200॥
1375.6: O Kabir, rendering the account is easy, if the heart is pure;
in that true court, no one seizes (him) by the hem. ॥201॥
1375.7: O Kabir, O duality, in earth and sky you are mighty and cannot be slain;
the followers of the six darshanas (the six schools of philosophy) and the eighty-four Siddhas have fallen into doubt (through you). ॥202॥
1375.8: O Kabir, nothing in me is mine; whatever there is, is yours;
in handing over to you what is yours, what does it cost me? ॥203॥
1375.9: O Kabir, saying you, you, I have become you; no I is left in me;
when (the line between) self and other was erased, wherever I look, there are you. ॥204॥
1375.10: O Kabir, (people) kept brooding on vices and nursing false hopes;
not one desire (of theirs) was fulfilled, and they rose and departed in despair. ॥205॥
1375.11: O Kabir, whoever remembers the Lord is at peace in the world;
one whom the Creator protects never wavers anywhere, here or hereafter. ॥206॥
1375.12: O Kabir, (we) were being crushed in the oil press; the True Guru set (us) free;
the devotion of long ages past came and showed itself. ॥207॥
1375.13: O Kabir, the day (of life) has passed in putting things off, and the interest goes on mounting;
the Lord has not been worshipped, the bond (of debt) has not been torn up, and death has arrived. ॥208॥
1375.14: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Kabir, the barking dog gets up and runs after carrion;
(but) by (God's) grace I have found the True Guru, who has set me free (from it). ॥209॥
1375.15: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Kabir, the land belongs to the Saadhs, (yet) thieves come in and sit down among (them);
the land does not feel (their) weight, and they reap gain upon gain. ॥210॥
1375.16: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Kabir, for the sake of the rice, the husk is beaten with the pestle;
(so too,) those who sit in evil company are then questioned by Dharam Raj. ॥211॥
1375.17: Tilochan says: O friend Nama, (you) are bewitched by Maya;
why do you print calico? Why do you not fix your mind on Ram? ॥212॥
1375.18: Nama says: O Tilochan, keep Ram on your lips;
do all your work with your hands and feet, (but keep) your mind with the Immaculate (Lord). ॥213॥
1376.1: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Kabir, no one is ours, and we are no one's;
(we) remain absorbed in him who made this creation. ॥214॥
1376.2: O Kabir, the flour fell into the mud, and nothing came to hand;
what was chewed while grinding and grinding — that alone stayed with (one). ॥215॥
1376.3: O Kabir, the mind knows all about it, and knowing, still does wrong;
what well-being is this, (when one) falls into the well with a lamp in hand? ॥216॥
1376.4: O Kabir, (my) love is fixed on the All-wise (Lord), (but) ignorant people forbid (me);
how can it go well, broken off from him to whom (this) soul and breath belong? ॥217॥
1376.5: O Kabir, why do you wear yourselves to death adorning houses and pavilions you are attached to?
The need is for three and a half cubits (of ground), or, (if) more, three and three-quarters. ॥218॥
1376.6: O Kabir, what I plan, (the Lord) does not do; what can come of my planning?
The Lord does what he himself has planned, which is not (even) in my mind. ॥219॥
1376.7: By the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
(God) himself brings on anxiety, and himself grants freedom from care;
O Nanak, let us praise him who takes care of all. ॥220॥
1376.8: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O Kabir, (the mortal) did not remember Ram, and wandered about in greed;
committing sins, he died; his span of life ran out in an instant. ॥221॥
1376.9: O Kabir, the body is an unbaked pitcher, made of nothing but raw clay;
if you would keep it whole, worship Ram; otherwise the matter is lost. ॥222॥
1376.10: O Kabir, let us keep calling Keshav, Keshav, and not sleep heedless;
calling out night and day, some day or other (he) will hear the cry. ॥223॥
1376.11: O Kabir, the body has become Kajli Ban (a dense forest), and the mind (in it) an elephant crazed with rut;
the jewel of (divine) knowledge is the goad, and the one who drives it is a rare Sant. ॥224॥
1376.12: O Kabir, (the Name of) Ram is the jewel, the mouth its purse; open (the purse) before one who can appraise it;
some customer will come along, who will buy it at a high price. ॥225॥
1376.13: O Kabir, (the mortal) did not know the Name of Ram, (but) reared a household as big as an army;
he died in his worldly affairs and nothing else, and not a sound (of him) came out beyond them. ॥226॥
1376.14: O Kabir, in blinks of the eyes, moment by moment, (life) has slipped away;
(yet) the mind does not let go of its entanglements; Jam has come and beaten the drum. ॥227॥
1376.15: O Kabir, Ram is (like) a tree, detachment its fruit;
the Saadh, who has given up wrangling and dispute, is its shade. ॥228॥
1376.16: O Kabir, sow such a seed as bears fruit all twelve months,
with cool shade and fruit in plenty, and birds sporting (in its branches). ॥229॥
1376.17: O Kabir, the giver is (like) a tree, compassion its fruit; he lives doing good to others;
the birds fly away to other lands, (yet) the tree goes on bearing good fruit. ॥230॥
1376.18: O Kabir, the company of the Saadh is gained (when it) is written on the forehead;
(through it) the gift of liberation is gained, and on the hard pass there is no barrier. ॥231॥
1377.1: O Kabir, one ghari (a measure of about twenty-four minutes), half a ghari, (or) half of the half —
whatever converse is held with the devotees, that is the gain. ॥232॥
1377.2: O Kabir, all the mortals who take hemp, fish and wine,
the pilgrimages, fasts and observances (they) have kept — all of these go down to Rasatal (the nether world). ॥233॥
1377.3: I keep my eyes lowered, holding the Friend within my heart;
I take every delight with my Beloved, and let no one see it. ॥234॥
1377.4: All eight watches (of day and night), all sixty-four gharis, my soul goes on gazing at you;
why should I lower my eyes? In every body I see the Beloved. ॥235॥
1377.5: Listen, my friend: does the soul dwell in the Beloved, or does the Beloved dwell in the soul?
I cannot tell soul and Beloved apart: is it the soul in the body, or the Beloved? ॥236॥
1377.6: O Kabir, the Brahmin is guru to the world, (but) to the devotees he is no guru;
tangled and entangled in the four Vedas, he has worn himself out to death. ॥237॥
1377.7: The Lord is sugar scattered in the sand; an elephant cannot pick it up;
says Kabir, the Guru has made (this) well understood: it is by becoming an ant that one eats it. ॥238॥
1377.8: O Kabir, if you long for (the game of) love, cut off your head and make it a ball;
playing on and on, lose yourself in ecstasy; then let come what may. ॥239॥
1377.9: O Kabir, if you long for (the game of) love, play with one who is ripe;
unripe mustard, crushed, has yielded neither oilcake nor oil. ॥240॥
1377.10: Searching, (people) stumble about like the blind, and do not recognise the Sants;
says Nama, how can God be found without the devotees? ॥241॥
1377.11: Those who leave a diamond such as the Lord and set their hopes on another,
those men will go to hell: Ravidas speaks the truth. ॥242॥
1377.12: O Kabir, if you keep a household, practise righteousness; if not, take up renunciation;
(if) a renunciant (then) takes on bonds, great is his misfortune. ॥243॥
